questions: How many WSe2/cTDBG devices did you fabricate and measure in all, and how many at each alignment angle showed the ν = −1 state and a C = +1 or C = 0 fan? Your p. 12 lists seven; were others measured?
Were any devices or cooldowns set aside (for example for contacts, gate leakage, or no ν = −1 state), and why?

Which displacement fields and field directions did you measure Landau fans at beyond D = 0.6 V/nm and B from 0 to 7 T, for D1 and D3, and does the C = +1 line from ν = −1 hold across the D range where the zero-field peak exists (Fig. 3e)?
What do the Landau fans and Rxy of D2 and D4, your second- and third-best Φ ≈ 0° devices, look like next to Fig. 4a–d, and how close to −h/e2 does Rxy get there?
Is Rxy in Fig. 4b,d antisymmetrized in field, and how does the "longitudinal admixture" that you mask near CNP in Fig. 4b enter along the ν = −1 trajectory where the 97.6% is read?

Could you show Rxy for D3 along the line where a C = +1 state from ν = −1 would run, and the CNP Landau levels of D3 next to those of D1, so the C = 0 assignment rests on Hall data from a device whose fans resolve? In Fig. 4f the CNP Landau levels are hard to make out.
Did you look for an anomalous Hall signal or field hysteresis at ν = −1 near B = 0 in the Φ ≈ 0° devices, and do you know the hBN-graphene alignment angles (or see hBN-moire peaks) in each device?

How was Φ checked independently of the Chern numbers, given that Methods (p. 13) use "the consistency of the measured Chern numbers across all aligned devices" as "a posteriori confirmation of the alignment assignment"?
